First spine check: City parcels vs NPCA ARN parcels

The check covers the full population of both layers, in EPSG:26917. The match is by representative point (point on surface) in both directions. The "overlap" set is the City parcels whose point lies within 5 m of an NPCA parcel. NPCA geometry was shifted by the measured median offset (dx +0.297 m, dy -0.939 m; NA-276).

189 NPCA parcels each contain the points of 2 or more City parcels, 2,538 City parcels in all. Here the City fabric is finer than NPCA's.
In the other direction, 275 NPCA rows reuse an ARN; one ARN sits on 49 polygons.

Recommended next steps for the HeavyMap ID registry
Mint parcel IDs from the City fabric.

per distinct City parcel geometry. Collapse the 83 stacked duplicates, keeping their OBJECTIDs as aliases. Use an opaque, permanent ID. Store a geometry fingerprint (rounded rep point plus area, in 26917) only as a matching aid for later re-pulls.
Register NPCA as an aligned source.
Record the translation (+0.297, -0.939 m) as a per-source transform in the registry, applied before every match. Attach ARN as a many-to-many attribute, with grades:
: reciprocal 1:1 with IoU of at least 0.9.
: the 189 NPCA parcels covering several City parcels.

from Addresses: one per number + street + community + unit, with points grouped under the civic address. Link each to its parcel by point-in-polygon, falling back to the nearest parcel within 10 m. Use Waste Collection as a cross-check of unit coverage.
from a footprint fingerprint. Link each building to the parcel of largest overlap, and keep the overlap list for the 21,307 that cross parcel lines.
